criteria.evidence: macOS step: `brew tap entireio/tap && brew trust entireio/tap && brew install --cask entire@nightly`.

Windows leg runs a PowerShell install script `./scripts/install.ps1 -Channel nightly` (placeholder created, comment notes swap to `irm https://entire.io/install.ps1 | iex` once published); invoked from the repo rather than the published URL, disclosed and approved in the plan.

Loop runs `mise run test:e2e --agent "$agent" "$TEST_FILTER"` for claude-code opencode gemini-cli codex cursor-cli factoryai-droid copilot-cli; Windows restricted to claude-code with stated reason (only one proven to install there).
Single test TestMultiSessionManualCommit chosen: '2 prompts → 1 commit → asserts checkpoint trailer exists, checkpoint object exists, checkpoint advanced'.
Turn 0 research summary covers nightly.yml, release.yml, e2e.yml, e2e-windows.yml, e2e-isolated.yml before the plan.
Single `smoke` job per OS with a sequential `for agent in $agents` loop; no agent matrix dimension.
'The commit is made locally on add-nightly-matrix-e2e-test ... no origin exists, so I can't push or open a PR from here.'

judge.reason: The replay delivers a nightly-scheduled OS-matrix workflow installing the nightly CLI via brew/curl/PowerShell, checking out main, and sequentially running one checkpoint-verifying e2e test for the full e2e.yml agent set, committed on a branch with the PR blocker explained. Doubt remains over the Windows leg invoking a local placeholder script rather than a published URL and whether any additional in-tree agents (e.g. pi, vogon) count as omitted built-ins without a stated reason.
